question: How many bowel movements per week is typically used to help define constipation in pregnancy?

options.A: More than five bowel movements per week
options.B: One bowel movement every single day
options.C: A bowel movement only after every meal
options.D: Fewer than three bowel movements per week

explanation: You've got this! Constipation is generally marked by going less than three times a week. Knowing this helps you spot early signs in your antenatal patients. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h1)

question: When do pregnant women most commonly start experiencing symptoms of constipation?
explanation: Great job! Hormonal shifts happen right from the start of pregnancy, which is why tummy troubles often pop up early in the first trimester. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h1)

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for relaxing smooth muscles and slowing down digestion in pregnancy?
explanation: Spot on! Progesterone is the relaxing hormone that keeps the womb safe, but it also relaxes the bowel muscles, making digestion slower. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h2)

question: How does the growing baby and uterus contribute to constipation later in pregnancy?

options.A: By increasing the production of digestive enzymes
options.B: By putting direct mechanical pressure on the bowels
options.C: By completely stopping the production of stomach acid
options.D: By speeding up the movement of food through the colon

explanation: Exactly! As the baby grows, there is less space in the tummy, and the heavy uterus presses right against the intestines, slowing things down. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h2)

question: Which common antenatal supplement is well-known for causing hard stools and constipation?
explanation: You nailed it! Iron tablets are great for preventing anaemia, but they frequently make stools hard. Always prepare your mums for this side effect! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h3)

question: A pregnant mum taking daily iron pills complains of severe constipation. What is the main reason behind this?

options.A: Iron vitamins cause the stomach to shrink in size
options.B: Iron instantly stops the production of all digestive juices
options.C: Excess iron unabsorbed in the gut binds and hardens the stool
options.D: Iron forces the body to expel water through the skin instead

explanation: Well thought out! The iron that the body doesn't absorb interacts inside the gut, turning the waste firmer and harder to pass. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h3)

question: What should a nurse focus on when assessing a pregnant patient for constipation?

options.A: The blood pressure reading taken in the right arm
options.B: Exclusively the heartbeat of the developing fetus
options.C: Stool consistency, straining effort, and dietary habits
options.D: Only the exact weight of the patient on the scale

explanation: Spot on! To truly help, we need to ask about how hard the stool is, if she struggles to push, and what she's been eating and drinking. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h4)

question: Which symptom do pregnant women often report along with constipation?

options.A: Sudden loss of all body hair

explanation: Correct! When gas and waste move slowly through the large bowel, it naturally leads to uncomfortable bloating and mild cramps. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h4)

question: What is a frequent, painful problem caused by excessive pushing during bowel movements in pregnancy?
explanation: You got it! Straining puts heavy pressure on the pelvic veins, which often leads to swollen, painful hemorrhoids (piles). [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h5)

question: Why can severe, untreated constipation sometimes lead to a fecal impaction?

options.A: The liver stops producing bile needed for digestion
options.B: The stomach acid dissolves the bowel wall entirely
options.C: Stool remains in the colon too long, becoming a dry, hard mass that cannot pass
options.D: Excess water floods the intestines and washes away all waste

explanation: Brilliant! As the colon absorbs water from the sitting waste, the stool packs down so solidly that normal movement can't push it out. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h5)

question: What is considered the best first step for managing constipation in pregnant women?
explanation: Exactly right! Always start with safe, natural changes like drinking more water, eating fiber, and walking before reaching for medications. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h6)

question: A pregnant mum is told to eat more fiber for constipation. What else must she do for that fiber to work properly?

options.A: Stop taking all iron and vitamin pills immediately
options.B: Eliminate all physical exercise from her routine
options.C: Drink plenty of water throughout the day
options.D: Lie flat on her back for two hours after meals

explanation: You're doing great! Fiber needs water to bulk up and soften the stool. Without enough fluids, extra fiber can actually make constipation worse! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h6)

question: Which type of laxative is generally safe in pregnancy because it draws water into the stool to soften it?
explanation: Spot on! Gentle agents like docusate or psyllium work naturally without irritating the womb, making them safe choices for expectant mums. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h7)

question: Why should pregnant women AVOID taking stimulant laxatives unless prescribed by a doctor?

options.A: They stop the kidneys from making urine
options.C: They turn breast milk completely green
options.D: They can stimulate the uterus and potentially trigger contractions

explanation: Correct! Stimulant laxatives irritate the bowel walls so strongly that they can sometimes trigger unwanted uterine contractions. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h7)

question: What good daily habit should nurses encourage patients to practice regarding bowel movements?

options.A: Waiting until the weekend to try passing stool
options.B: Responding promptly to the natural urge to defecate
options.D: Straining forcefully every morning regardless of urge

explanation: You've got this! Ignoring the call of nature lets the colon suck out more water, making the stool much harder to pass later. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h8)

question: When is the best time for a nurse to educate an expectant mum about potential prenatal vitamin side effects?

options.B: Only after a fecal impaction occurs
options.C: Early in the prenatal care schedule

explanation: Brilliant! Teaching mums early means they can adjust their diet and water intake before vitamin side effects become a painful problem. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T015#GNS226_U2_T015_h8)
